Four corpora · rebuilt dataset

Chuvash stress, phonetics and phonology

What four corpora say about the vowel system, the phonotactics, syllable weight and where stress falls — and which of the standard descriptions survive measurement.

CorpusSourceSizeRole here
Chuvash Electronic WordlistZheltov 200818,984 typestype inventory, minimal word
Chuvash Monolingual corpusPlotnikov 20242.9M sentencestoken frequency, alternations
Common Voice ChuvashArdila 2020; Ahn 202217,329 clips · 104 speakersspeaker-varied acoustics
Chuvash VoicePlotnikov 202429,727 clips · ~1 speakerbulk acoustics, consonant length

MFA 3.4 (Vox Communis chuvash_mfa); vowels measured with new-FAVE, f0 and intensity with Praat, consonant durations from the pre-recode grids. 574,344 vowel tokens and 1,424,952 phone tokens after cleaning.

What the standard descriptions claim

Four claims this study can test, and one it cannot.

ClaimSourceVerdict here
Stress falls on the rightmost full vowelKrueger 1961; Dobrovolsky 1999supported, with a stressless default
Reduced vowels may round, especially under stressgrammarsrefuted for ⟨ӗ⟩; untestable for ⟨ӑ⟩ ⟨ы⟩
High row is front/back × rounded/unroundedKrueger 1961front row confirmed; back row undecidable
Geminates resist intervocalic lenitiongrammarsgeminates are phonetically long
Two vowels cannot occur in successiongrammarsconsistent with the phonotactics
The reduced vowels are the crux. Whether ⟨ы⟩ /ʉ/ belongs with the full vowels or the reduced ones changes which syllable every rule predicts, so the inventory and the default have to be settled separately — and only one kind of evidence bears on each.

Inventory question

Settled on the written corpora: minimal word and positional restriction. Acoustics cannot settle it without circularity.

Default question

Settled on the acoustics of polysyllabic all-reduced words — the only configuration where the two defaults disagree.

newThe default question, with the utterance edge removed

A stresses the leftmost reduced vowel; B leaves the word stressless. 24,223 all-reduced polysyllabic word tokens, 37,824 vowels.

In a disyllable, “non-initial” is the final syllable — and the final syllable of an utterance-final word is 63% longer. So the raw contrast is mostly a measurement of the edge, and f0 is mostly declination. Refitting with word-final position, utterance-final position and position-in-utterance in the model:

CueRawEdges controlledtJND
duration-19.6 ms+0.59 ms0.6410 ms
intensity+1.84 dB-0.20 dB-1.863 dB
f0+12.4 Hz-2.52 Hz-4.171 Hz

No cue makes the initial syllable prominent. f0 clears its nominal threshold in the wrong direction, by 0.02 semitones on a 200 Hz voice; 1 Hz is a laboratory floor for steady tones, not a threshold for running speech.

Verdict: default B — rightmost full vowel, else stressless — on three times the sample the filtered estimate rested on.

Duration ranks B first, intensity ranks A first — Dobrovolsky's asymmetry

Mixed models over the whole dataset, one per rule per measure, with vowel quality, coda, utterance position, speech rate and word frequency controlled and (1|speaker) + (1|file_name) + (1|word_label).

RuleΔ AIC, durationβ durationΔ AIC, intensityβ intensity (dB)β f0 (st)
A6777+0.09600+0.523+0.463
A5695+0.096621+0.508+0.459
A4678+0.096441+0.494+0.458
B6209+0.113697+0.512+0.517
B50+0.1181116+0.506+0.522
B471+0.1176128+0.497+0.522

Duration puts B5 first by 695 AIC over the best A rule; intensity puts A6 first by 97 over the best B rule. This is the asymmetry Dobrovolsky (1999) reported on 80 vowels, reproduced on 499,357.

Three reasons not to read this table as the answer. (1) The intensity coefficients are 0.49–0.52 dB against a 3 dB JND — six to seven times too small to hear. Statistically overwhelming, perceptually nothing. (2) The three cues DISAGREE about which rule wins — duration and f0 rank B first, intensity ranks A first — so no single column settles it, and that disagreement is itself a finding rather than noise to be averaged away. (3) The ranking is dominated by the ~90% of words where all six rules agree; see the conflict-subset slide.

The final baseline is deliberately NOT in this table. Its predictor 1{sidx == sN} is identical to syl_final on all 574,344 rows (φ = 1.0000), so against a linear position trend it is unidentified: omit the control and it absorbs the whole edge effect, include it and no residual variation is left. It becomes testable only with position entered nonparametrically, and when it is, its intensity coefficient is negative — quieter than trend. See the word-edge slide.

newOrthographic geminates are phonetically long

Intervocalic, word-medial position; 22,580 long against 149,071 singleton tokens, Chuvash Voice.

Consonant durations do not exist in the analysis dataset — it carries vowels. They come from the pre-recode grids, because stage 5 collapses nine of the fourteen long consonants. The pre-recode grids agree with the recoded ones on 100% of interval boundaries.

Across the 10 measurable places the ratio runs 1.11–1.71, median 1.32.

Two places are excluded, not reported as short geminates. The aligner has a hard floor at 30 ms, and 100% of /vː/ tokens and 43% of /mː/ sit exactly on it. The words are genuine geminates (сиввӗн, кӗвви, уйрӑммӑнах); the durations were clipped, not measured.

Common Voice cannot contribute. Its only pre-recode grids are a different third-party alignment — 18.9% boundary agreement with the grids the measurements come from. Everything here is one speaker reading prose.

retractedWord-finally, a long consonant and a reduced vowel trade off

Your question: does a final geminate plus a reduced vowel differ from a singleton plus a full vowel? 2 × 2 with the consonant's identity, word length, utterance edge and pause controlled.

Final shapeAdjusted rhyme duration
short C + full V+0.0%
long C + full V+19.3%
short C + reduced V-7.1%
long C + reduced V+11.2%

The two effects are additive — interaction t = 0.30. Lengthening the consonant and reducing the vowel are independent, roughly equal and opposite adjustments to the same total.

What that means

Long C + reduced V comes out +11.2% against short C + full V — about 7 ms on a 160 ms rhyme, under the 10 ms JND.

RETRACTED. This was presented as positive weight evidence — a shared timing budget, i.e. a mora. It is not. Two additive effects of similar size landing on the same total is consistent with a shared budget but does not distinguish it from two independent adjustments that happen to be comparable; and the net difference sits under the 10 ms JND, so the configuration a mora predicts is also the configuration no difference predicts. Only designed elicitation can separate them.

пулӑ 'fish' ~ пулли 'its fish': the stem-final reduced vowel disappears and the consonant geminates. Candidate zero-mora vowel.

The class was identified from text alone, so there is no acoustic circularity: for every corpus type ending in ӑ/ӗ after a consonant, is stem + C + C + и attested? Of 52,582 candidates, 1,484 (2.8%) have the geminate form — and the method recovers the right words:

A correction worth keeping. Without the consonant control the final vowel came out 5% shorter (t = −2.41). That was entirely place of articulation: the alternating class is dominated by л р н ҫ т. Sentence type from the transcript's final punctuation; f0 in semitones relative to each speaker's own median.

Clitic-marked polar questions are the only group that rises. wh-questions carry a statement contour. Unmarked questions sit between.

The enclitic -и is homophonous with the third-person possessive, so the label is orthographic. Two checks license it: a sentence-final -и appears in 28.0% of questions against 0.95% of statements; and statements whose last word ends in -и behave exactly like all other statements, so the string alone does nothing.

nullCodas never attract prominence; sonority survives only in duration

Within-word design: 527,444 vowels in 256,239 polysyllabic word tokens. Each word is a stratum, so word frequency, length, speaker and speech rate cannot confound.

/a/ is 20 ms longer and 2 dB louder than the high vowels for reasons unconnected with stress, so every test is run twice — raw, and after removing the vowel's own mean.

Predicts being the most prominent syllableduration, rawduration, intrinsic removedintensity, rawintensity, intrinsic removed
closed syllable0.6610.6531.1481.146
the vowel /a/2.0711.3482.3671.119
a non-high vowel1.5281.1662.0380.958

Coda odds are below 1 on duration and flat on intensity — and under a rule-based definition of stress they are 0.848 (B5) and 0.838 (A6). The two sonority predictors must be read separately, because they do not behave alike: /a/ survives intrinsic correction on duration at 1.348 and still carries 2.367 on intensity, while non-high gives 1.166 on duration and 2.038 — i.e. null — on intensity. Only the non-high row vanishes in intensity.

Sonority-sensitivity holds at an odds ratio of 1.35 for /a/ on duration, not the 2–3 the raw measures suggest — a real effect and a modest one. Whether it reaches intensity depends on which predictor you ask: /a/ yes (2.37), non-high no (2.04).

166,749 non-primary syllables in words of three or more syllables.

Duration falls monotonically towards the primary, then rises after it — but there is no every-other-syllable alternation, and the two measures have opposite signs: syllables after the primary are longer and at the same time quieter. Stress lengthens and raises intensity together; this is final lengthening.

revisedRounding: established for the two front vowels, for neither back one

HEIGHT-MATCHED pairs. The previous version used one anchor per harmony series — /i/ front, /a/ back — which compared mid ⟨ӥ⟩ against high /i/ and mid ⟨ә⟩ against low /a/, confounding rounding with height.

/y/ ⟨ӳ⟩ vs /i/ ⟨и⟩-0.483-21.2-0.457rounded

The control is not a result

The /u/~/ɔ/ row presupposes Krueger's description of that pair. It cannot be cited as evidence that ⟨ы⟩ is unrounded or ⟨у⟩ rounded. An earlier version of this deck said “Krueger's high row is confirmed exactly” — that was circular and is withdrawn.

A small control effect is also ambiguous between “F3 is a weak cue to back rounding” and “these two vowels differ less in rounding than described”.

Why ⟨ә⟩ is undecidable

Structural, not a power problem: the inventory contains no mid back unrounded vowel to serve as its height-matched anchor. Settling it needs lip video or another articulatory measure.

The formant space recovers the harmony classes, not the eight phonemes

Gaussian mixtures on F1–F3 at the vowel midpoint, non-palatal contexts, compared against the phonemic labels.

Agreement peaks at k = 5 (ARI 0.416) and is markedly worse at eight (0.286). BIC falls monotonically to k = 12 in both context sets and is uninformative — it is reported, not mined.

At the peak the clusters are front harmony (/i e y ø/ together), back non-low (/ʉ u ɵ/) and /a/ on its own. That is the harmony partition, not the phoneme inventory.

This is not an argument that Chuvash has five vowels. There are phonemic minimal pairs for eight qualities. It is an argument that midpoint formants are the wrong measurement to read an inventory off — see the next slide.

The eight qualities are recoverable — from context, not formants

Gradient boosting, balanced accuracy, 40,000-token samples. Folds grouped by word type, so a model given the neighbouring segments cannot memorise words.

Featuresall eight/i/ vs /y//ʉ/ vs /ɵ/
formants only (F1 F2 F3)0.4690.6060.588
+ duration0.4910.6110.613
+ neighbouring segments0.6430.7130.833
+ word harmony class0.6750.7570.833
chance0.1250.5000.500

Formants alone give 0.47 on the eight-way problem. Adding the neighbouring segments takes it to 0.64; duration adds almost nothing. The two crowded pairs go from 0.61 and 0.59 to 0.71 and 0.83.

This is what a language with vowel harmony and pervasive consonant palatalisation should look like: the vowel's identity is partly distributed onto its neighbours. A midpoint-formant inventory undercounts it by construction.

Harmony class is partly circular as a feature — the claim rests on the neighbouring-segment step, which is not.

The first-syllable restriction tracks vowel height, not weight

Percentage of each vowel's polysyllabic tokens that fall in the first syllable.

Vowel/ʉ//u//y//i//a//ɵ//ø//e/
% in syllable 196.289.680.947.230.529.227.712.3
% closed52.052.931.635.643.649.439.338.1

The four high vowels occupy the top four positions (47–96%); the non-high vowels are all below 30%. Closed-syllable rate does not order the same way, so the restriction is about height, not weight.

Consequence for the inventory question: this pattern cannot be used to group ⟨ы⟩ /ʉ/ with the reduced vowels. /ʉ/ is the most restricted vowel in the language (96.2%), but so is /u/ (89.6%) and /y/ (80.9%), and nobody calls those reduced. The minimal-word evidence has to carry it.

The minimal-word evidence, and why the corpus cannot settle it alone

Which vowels can stand in an open monosyllable — the test that separates inventory 5 from inventory 6.

In the wordlist, /y/ forms open monosyllables at 15.4% (8 of 52 types) while /ʉ/ forms none (0 of 37), /ø/ none (0 of 90), and /ɵ/ 1.1% (2 of 175, both Zheltov's own ӑ and хӑ). The full-versus-reduced gap on the minimal-word measure is largest under inventory 5.

The monolingual corpus appears to contradict this, and it is wrong. It shows open monosyllables with reduced vowels at 9.7–28.1% — but those types are de-hyphenated line breaks and letter-spaced emphasis, not words: нӑ 17,003, тӑ 12,398, лӑ 11,814, нӗ 10,985. They are phonotactically legal, so no phonotactic filter removes them. Only dictionary attestation does.

The corpus can carry token frequency claims. It cannot carry type inventory claims.

Who is actually speaking

Chuvash Voice ships no speaker identity. 24 acoustic features per recording (f0 quantiles, 16-band mean-centred LTAS, HNR), clustered in PCA space with the same/different threshold calibrated on Common Voice's 109 known speakers.

Common Voice

78
clusters, largest 34.8%

109 known speakers — the calibration set.

Chuvash Voice

99.4%
of recordings in one cluster

93.4% when every recording is assigned to its nearest centroid. Effectively one speaker.

Minor voices

3–4
other speakers, 6.6% of recordings

Four clusters at 108–144 Hz against a 226 Hz dominant voice.

The gender metadata is not credible. The dominant Chuvash Voice voice sits at 225.7 Hz and is labelled male_masculine. In Common Voice, where the labels are self-reported, male voices average 125.5 Hz and female 223.6 Hz.

Consequence: one speaker supplies about 69% of all vowels, and five cover 90%. Every model here carries (1|speaker) + (1|file_name) + (1|word_label), and no cross-speaker generalisation is claimed from Chuvash Voice alone.

The segment inventory, including 14 long consonants

From the aligned grids: 9 vowels (8 native plus the loan /o/) and 20 consonant places, 14 of them attested long.

Long consonant/lː//nː//ɕː//tː//sː//kː//rː//ʃː/

33,315 long-consonant tokens, 1.7–2.0% of all phones. /lː/ is 10.2% of all /l/; /ɕː/ is 8.3% of all /ɕ/.

Stage 5 of the pipeline destroys most of this. chuvash_phonology.py collapses eight long consonants to singletons (26,832 tokens); five others survive only because they are absent from its map. Everything in this deck about length comes from the pre-recode grids.

Vowel token shares agree closely across the four corpora — the largest spread is 3.6 points, for /e/ (14.7–18.3%), then /ɵ/ at 2.7.

Phonotactics: CV and CVC, and almost nothing else

Syllable shapewordlistmonolingualspoken

Over 90% of syllables are CV or CVC in all three sources; complex onsets are under 1%. Words begin with a vowel 14–18% of the time and end with one 45–51%.

The syllabifier in the repository does not do what the manuscript says it does. max_onset_size() returns 1 for any cluster and ignores the sonority table entirely, which diverges from the documented algorithm on 20–26% of word types. The shipped behaviour is linguistically correct for Chuvash — the documented algorithm would license /kr/ /pl/ /ml/ /ʃn/ onsets the language disallows. The Methods prose needs rewriting, not the code.

The eight vowels, speaker-normalised, non-palatal contexts

Lobanov within speaker; 447,719 tokens. Non-palatal excludes vowels adjacent to /j ɕ ʃ tɕ ʒ/, which front F2 enough to smear the space.

The means separate cleanly. The distributions do not — which is why the midpoint-formant clustering on slide 12 undercounts, and why the contrast has to be looked for in context rather than in the vowel itself.

methodWhat the rebuild changed, and why it matters

The cleaning step used to delete rows outside Tukey fences computed within vowel × corpus. Those fences preferentially removed long vowels — which is to say, the stressed ones.

Two published conclusions were withdrawn as a direct result of readmitting those rows. That is the strongest argument that readmitting them was right.

Both filters are now flags, not deletions (iqr_outlier_any, word_complete), and the fences are computed within vowel × speaker. Every analysis reports the full sample, and the coda and sonority tests report the strict subset alongside so the reader can see the nulls do not depend on the choice.

newThe best-identified result: duration steps up into the stressed syllable

Within-word steps between adjacent syllables, stratified on (word length × syllable index × target vowel). A within-word difference cancels the word, recording and speaker levels exactly, so no declination baseline has to be specified.

Cuestep INTO the stressed syllabletstep OUT of ittJND
duration+21.32 ms17.2-13.58 ms-5.910 ms (Hirsh 1959) — cleared
intensity-0.14 dB-1.13-0.16 dB-0.663 dB (Moore 2007) — null
f0+0.361 st7.2+0.248 st2.9both steps UP, so no peak

Why it is not circular

Designation at syllable i depends on whether anything to the right of i holds a full vowel. That information is in neither the step nor the strata. This is the only specification that holds local vowel quality fixed and still recovers the rule.

Stratifying matters: with the vowel as an additive covariate the estimate is +17.95 ms, and at word-final position designation is a deterministic function of the target's own vowel, so part of that figure is a full-versus-reduced comparison in disguise.

The ceiling on this design

Only 15 strata contain the same vowel at the same position in words of the same length on both sides of the designation contrast. That is the structural limit, not a sampling accident: it is the same ceiling the matched-vowel design hit.

Descriptively the largest duration step up in the word lands on the designated syllable in 9 of 9 testable cells, at +20 to +36 ms, with pre-tonic syllables carrying negative steps.

nullThe post-tonic intensity drop is position, not stress

Two hypotheses about contour shape. The duration one holds; the intensity one does not survive its own control.

Held: the stressed syllable is the first to lengthen

“Leftmost syllable above the word's own mean duration” identifies the designated syllable where stress is left of the edge (pre-antepenultimate 0.843 against 0.250 chance; antepenultimate 0.708 against 0.333), and the mirror statistic does not. Where stress is final it reverses.

Failed: a drop after the stressed syllable

Raw, the designation effect on the following intensity step is −1.735 dB. With both vowels controlled it is −0.315 dB (t −1.19), and the mirror control vanishes symmetrically. The step out of the designated syllable is a rise in all five cells where that syllable is syllable 1 and a fall in all four where it is syllable 2 or later — which just restates the syllable-2 intensity peak.

The class that separates the two anchorings settles it: in 3-syllable antepenultimate words (1,773 tokens) the step out of the designated first syllable is +0.43 dB, and the drop arrives at the word edge instead. In the penultimate class the post-tonic syllable is the word-final one, so that class cannot distinguish them at all.

Worth keeping, though: a drop can be an informative perceptual cue without being an independent correlate. It is audible and it does co-locate with stress in the penultimate class. That is a claim about perception this corpus cannot test — and it is a different claim from the one the numbers reject.

newf0, the third cue — never tested before now

f0 at the vowel midpoint (mean of steps 10 and 11, the exact analogue of the adopted intensity measure), in semitones from the speaker's own median. 98.1% of vowels usable; 3,518 octave-tracking errors removed. Within-speaker normalisation makes the open question about the Chuvash Voice speaker's sex moot downstream.

Two of three cues now favour B

duration B5 first · f0 B6/B5/B4 first · intensity A6 first. The stressless-word analysis gains its second independent cue.

No syllable-2 f0 peak

f0 peaks on syllable 1 at every word length, and syllable 2 is lower at every length (-0.10, -0.64, -0.31, -0.17, -0.30 st for lengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). So the syllable-2 effect is intensity-only: duration peaks word-finally, f0 word-initially.

revisedThe word-final rise is a boundary tone, not stress

A conclusion from earlier in this project was wrong and is corrected here.

Word-final syllable, relative to trenddurationintensityf0
pooled+11.70 ms-0.765 dB+6.11 Hz
word-internal+6.99 ms+0.048 dB+10.82 Hz
utterance-final+45.63 ms-5.997 dB-21.41 Hz

Earlier this was reported as “longer but quieter than trend” and counted against final stress on the grounds that the cues disagree. With f0 in hand it is longer, quieter and higher — two of three cues in the stress direction.

But the f0 elevation reverses sign at the utterance edge (+10.82 Hz word-internally, -21.41 Hz utterance-finally, interaction t −179). Lexical stress cannot flip sign according to whether the word ends the utterance; a boundary tone does exactly that. So final stress is still unsupported — the reason is now “it is a boundary tone”, not “the cues disagree”.

Why final can be tested at all: 1{sidx == sN} is identical to syl_final on all 574,344 rows (φ = 1.0000), so it is unidentified against a linear trend. Entering position NONPARAMETRICALLY makes the predicate a deterministic but nonlinear function of position, and that is what identifies it. initial stays unidentified.

newThe duration peak walks leftward with the rightmost full vowel

Shape classes defined by from_end = sN − (position of the rightmost full vowel), not by strict full/reduced strings, so RFFR, RRFR and FRFR join FFFR in the penultimate class. Computed under both the 5-full and 6-full inventories.

The observed duration peak sits on exactly the syllable the rule designates in 12 of 12 word-length × class cells containing a full vowel — identically under both inventories. The intensity peak matches in only 4 of 12; it sits on syllable 2 in 13 of 14 cells, so it tracks position rather than the rule.

A5 or A6?

The coding is the 5-full inventory (a e i u y), i.e. A5/B5. Adding /ɔ/ ⟨ы⟩ moves 2.1% of word tokens, almost all of them disyllables leaving the stressless class for the initially-stressed one — because ⟨ы⟩ is overwhelmingly first-syllable. The peak-match result is identical either way, so these profiles do not adjudicate A5 against A6.

The controlled version does not test this

Net of vowel quality the longest syllable is word-final in 13 of 14 cells — but that model has vowel_label as a covariate, and the rule's designation is defined on vowel fullness, so it adjusts away the rule's own content. Its failure is not evidence against the rule. The step design above is the controlled test.

newThe suffixation confound, cleared

The reduced vowels that define the right edge of the penultimate and antepenultimate classes are overwhelmingly suffixal, so “the rightmost full vowel is the penult” and “this word carries a suffix” are nearly the same statement. No corpus here has morphological annotation, so the parse was induced.

Duration step up into the stressed syllablemststeps
all words+21.3717.330,878
no suffix parsed+19.1211.310,049
suffix parsed+22.3913.620,543

The effect is present and nearly as large in words with no suffix parsed, and the designation × suffixal-status interaction is null (-0.65 ms, t -0.27). So the rule is not a stem-edge rule in disguise.

A separate finding: at the same position with the same vowel, a suffixal syllable is +6.73 ms longer (t 4.0) and -0.70 dB quieter (t -4.0) than a stem syllable, independent of stress.

The parse, and what it is not

Signature induction over 430,008 types on the phonemic form, using no vowel-quality information — essential, or it would reproduce the shape classes it is meant to check. Cut fixed at 500 stems by F1 against a reference suffix list: recall 0.817, precision 0.561, 111 suffixes accepted.

Only suffixes of ≥2 phonemes are parsed, because string recurrence cannot tell a genitive -n from a stem-final n. So the monomorphemic class is really “no confident parse”. That contaminates it with genuinely suffixed words and therefore biases this test against finding a difference.

The reference list has not been checked by a Chuvash specialist and the per-word error rate is not measured. әкәр 'bread' is wrongly split. Both need review.

The confound is real and large as a descriptive fact: outside the word-final class the designated syllable coincides with the last stem syllable 92.0% of the time in the penultimate class, against a 45.9% chance rate of being suffixal. It just does not drive the acoustics.

What a reviewer will press on

  • Chuvash Voice is one speaker. 99.4% of its recordings fall in a single voice cluster, and it supplies about 69% of all vowels. Cross-speaker claims can only come from Common Voice's 104.
  • Gemination rests on that one speaker. Common Voice's only pre-recode grids are a different alignment, so consonant length is unreplicated across speakers.
  • f0 is stylised to 2 semitones. Nothing smaller than a couple of semitones should be rested on. The question-intonation result is several semitones and safe; the stress-related f0 differences are not.
  • Intensity was measured on excised vowels. Praat wrote 71% of the 20 step cells as literal 0.0 — undefined, not silence — and the script raised the pitch floor for short vowels, making the analysis window duration-dependent. int_midpoint is the only defensible column; total_intensity is a duration measure (r = 0.909 with duration).
  • Sonority is real but modest. Odds ratio 1.35 for /a/ after intrinsic correction, not the 2.1 the raw measure shows, and only in duration.
  • The alignment was not hand-checked. A stratified hand-check of ~250 vowels and a cross-alignment confidence score are specified in alignment_confidence.md and not yet run.
  • The moraic split has no phonetic support here. The пулӑ~пулли alternation is recoverable from text but not from these three acoustic measures. The weight evidence is the additive long-C/reduced-V trade-off, not the alternation.
Every number in this deck is generated from 9-analyze/output/*.csv by analyses/make_slides.py, so it cannot drift from the analyses. Provenance for each run is in 9-analyze/data/run_log/.
